meta.name: Triage and draft support replies using Anthropic and Google Sheets

name: Three-agent support desk: triage, research your docs, draft a reply, human gate

parameters.content:
## Three-agent support desk: triage, research your docs, draft a reply, human gate

### How it works

This workflow triages an inbound support ticket, researches it against your own documentation, and drafts a reply, using three separate agents so each has a narrow job it can do reliably. A credential check runs before any drafting, and a final gate decides whether the draft is safe to send automatically or needs a person. Every outcome is written to Google Sheets, and tickets the documentation could not answer raise a separate gap note.

### Setup steps

- Add Anthropic credentials to the three chat model nodes used by the triage, research, and drafting agents.
- Fill the configuration node with product context, severity definitions, tone guide, docs base URL, auto-send ceiling, and the notification webhook URL.
- Connect the Google Sheets node to the spreadsheet and sheet used as the ticket ledger.
- Point the documentation search tool at a docs site that returns readable HTML.
- Copy the webhook production URL into your helpdesk, or post a JSON body containing text, email, and subject fields.
- Run manually once with the sample ticket before connecting a live queue.

### Customization

Start with the auto-send ceiling at the lowest severity and widen it once you have reviewed real drafts. You can also adjust the severity definitions, tone guide, and ledger columns, or point the notification steps at a different channel.

## Receive and normalize tickets

Accepts inbound tickets from the webhook or builds a sample ticket for manual runs, then normalizes both paths into one consistent shape.

## Triage the ticket

Classifies category, severity, sentiment, and whether the text contains a credential, following the severity definitions from the configuration node.

## Credential hold and documentation research

Holds tickets containing an apparent credential with a fixed reply, and sends everything else to a research agent that reads your documentation over HTTP.

## Draft the reply and gate it

Drafts a response from the research findings only, then checks confidence, documentation coverage, and severity before allowing an automatic send.

## Human review gate

Pauses the execution until a reviewer chooses to send, rewrite, or escalate, recording each decision separately so the drafts can be measured later.

## Log and flag documentation gaps

Writes every outcome to the ledger sheet, then raises a separate note whenever the documentation could not answer the ticket.

nodes.name: Ticket Received Webhook
nodes.notes: POST {text, email, subject}. Copy the production URL into your helpdesk.

nodes.name: Set Configuration Fields
nodes.notes: severityDefinitions and toneGuide are read into the prompts verbatim — vague definitions produce vague triage.

assignments.name: productContext
assignments.value: A production-planning tool for small manufacturers. Users create orders, assign them to machines, and track progress on a shop-floor screen. Common areas: order import, scheduling, shop-floor display, user permissions, reporting.

assignments.name: severityDefinitions
assignments.value: critical = production is stopped or data is lost. high = a core workflow is broken but a workaround exists. normal = something behaves incorrectly without blocking work. low = cosmetic, or a how-do-I question. needs_info = cannot tell without more detail.

assignments.name: toneGuide
assignments.value: Plain language, no corporate padding. Short paragraphs. Say what we know and what we do not. Never open with 'We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience'.

assignments.name: testTicketText
assignments.value: Hi, since this morning the shop floor screen shows yesterday's orders instead of today's. Refreshing does not help. We can still see the right list in the admin panel.

options.systemMessage:
=You are the first-line triage system for an inbound support queue. You read ONE ticket and classify it. You do NOT answer it — a later specialist agent does that.

PRODUCT CONTEXT:
{{ $('Set Configuration Fields').first().json.productContext }}

SEVERITY DEFINITIONS (use these exactly, not your own intuition):
{{ $('Set Configuration Fields').first().json.severityDefinitions }}

CLASSIFY ON:
- `category`: which part of the product this concerns.
- `severity`: strictly by the definitions above.
- `sentiment`: how the customer sounds — this affects tone later, never severity.
- `is_question_vs_bug`: are they confused about how it works, or is something broken?
- `contains_credentials`: true if the ticket text appears to contain a password, API key, token or similar. This is important — flagged tickets skip automated drafting entirely.

RULES:
- An angry tone does NOT raise severity. A calm report of total data loss is still critical.
- If the ticket is too vague to classify, set severity to 'needs_info' and say what is missing in `missing_info` rather than guessing.
- Keep all structured fields in English regardless of the ticket's language.

parameters.text: =Research this ticket against the docs: {{ $('Process Triage Results').first().json.one_line_summary }}

options.systemMessage:
=You research a support ticket against the team's own documentation before anyone drafts a reply. You do NOT write the customer-facing answer — that is the next agent's job.

TICKET: {{ $('Process Triage Results').first().json.one_line_summary }}
CATEGORY: {{ $('Process Triage Results').first().json.category }}

Use `search_docs` to find the relevant documentation pages. Try several phrasings — the customer's words rarely match the docs' words. Follow links between pages when a page references another.

RULES:
- Only cite pages you actually fetched. Never invent a URL or a doc section.
- If the docs genuinely do not cover this, say so in `docs_gap` and set `found_answer` to false. That is a useful finding, not a failure — it tells the team what to write next.
- Distinguish between 'the docs explain this' and 'I inferred this'. Anything inferred goes in `inferred_notes`, clearly separated.
- Stop after {{ $('Set Configuration Fields').first().json.maxDocPages }} pages.

nodes.name: Search Documents HTTP Request
nodes.notes: Plain HTTP — no docs-platform API needed. The url field uses n8n's documented placeholder syntax ={url}; some validators flag this as an invalid URL — it is correct, do not 'fix' it to a literal address. Client-side-rendered docs sites return little; the agent reports that as a gap rather than inventing an answer.

parameters.elementsToOmit: script, style, nav, footer, svg, noscript
parameters.toolDescription: Fetch one documentation page and return its readable text. Takes a full URL including https://. Use it to search the product documentation — start at the docs base URL, then follow links or guess likely paths such as /guides, /faq, /troubleshooting. A 404 on a guessed path is harmless, just try another.

parameters.text:
=Draft a reply to this ticket:

{{ $('Normalize Ticket Data').first().json.ticket_text }}

nodes.name: Evaluate Auto-Send Safety
nodes.notes: All three must hold: high confidence AND docs found an answer AND severity is at the configured ceiling. Deliberately strict.

nodes.name: Post to Reviewer Webhook
nodes.notes: Carries the three review links. No-op if notifyWebhookUrl is blank.

nodes.name: Await Human Review Decision
nodes.notes: Pauses until Send / Rewrite / Escalate is clicked. See the Risk sticky.

parameters.jsCode:
const t = $json;
return [{ json: {
  logged_at: new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 19).replace('T', ' '),
  ticket_id: t.ticket_id || '',
  received_at: t.received_at || '',
  customer_email: t.customer_email || '',
  subject: t.subject || '',
  category: t.category || '',
  severity: t.severity || '',
  sentiment: t.sentiment || '',
  is_question_vs_bug: t.is_question_vs_bug || '',
  contains_credentials: String(!!t.contains_credentials),
  one_line_summary: t.one_line_summary || '',
  found_answer: String(!!t.found_answer),
  docs_gap: t.docs_gap || '',
  relevant_doc_urls: t.relevant_doc_urls || '',
  confidence_in_draft: t.confidence_in_draft || '',
  confidence_reason: t.confidence_reason || '',
  final_route: t.final_route || '',
  human_decision: t.human_decision || '',
  draft_reply: t.draft_reply || '',
  internal_note: t.internal_note_for_agent || '',
} }];
